description: A feedback delay whose time is a grid step of a clock, with damping in the loop and a pitch input that turns it into a Karplus-Strong string

params.text: Picks the delay length as a fraction of the beat, in thirteen steps from eight beats at the counter-clockwise end down to a five-hundred-and-twelfth of one at the clockwise end
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the TIME input before it is added to the TIME knob
Sets how much of the delay output goes back into it, from 0.95 inverted at the counter-clockwise end through no feedback at the centre to 0.95 at the clockwise end
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the FEEDBACK input before it is added to the FEEDBACK knob
Sets the base delay time, from 20ms to 2 seconds, that the TIME fraction multiplies while no clock is patched; with a clock patched nothing in the module reads it, despite the panel printing GLITCH
Damps the repeats, setting how much of the top end the feedback path keeps each time round
Crossfades the dry input against the delayed signal on an equal-power curve
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the GLITCH input before it is added to the GLITCH knob

inputs.text: The audio input into the delay line
A clock here sets the beat the delay fraction is measured against, taken from rising edges above 1V; when it stops for more than two beats the module falls back to the GLITCH knob for its base time
Moves the delay fraction, scaled by its attenuverter, with 5V covering the whole of the TIME knob's travel
Moves the feedback amount, scaled by its attenuverter, with 5V covering the whole of the FEEDBACK knob's travel
A rising edge above 1V starts the delay line again from empty, crossfading into it over the crossfade time set on the menu
Sets the delay length from a pitch instead, one volt per octave from C4 at 261.63Hz, which plays the delay as a plucked string; below the crossover frequency on the menu it is ignored
Moves the base delay time, scaled by its attenuverter, with 5V covering the whole of the GLITCH knob's travel; with a clock patched it changes nothing

outputs.text: The delayed signal mixed with the dry input, five times the internal signal level and clipped at 10V

notes: with nothing patched to CLK the delay time comes from the knob printed GLITCH, which is the only thing that knob does; a clock at CLK takes that job over and leaves the knob inert
menu: Delay units: Straight, Triplet, Dotted — reads the beat as straight, triplet or dotted note lengths, which scales every step the TIME knob can take
Crossfade time — sets how long the delay takes to fade from its old length into a new one
KS / clock crossover — sets the frequency above which a pitch at the 1V/OCT input takes the delay length over; below it that input does nothing
